# fileseek

Moves a file pointer.

```ttl
fileseek <file handle> <offset> <origin>
```

## Remarks

Moves the pointer for the file specified by &lt;file handle&gt;.
With this command, the file pointer is moved to following:

<table>
 <tr>
  <th>&lt;origin&gt;</th>
  <td>0</td>
  <td>&lt;offset&gt; bytes from the beginning of the file.</td>
 </tr>
 <tr>
  <th>&lt;origin&gt;</th>
  <td>1</td>
  <td>&lt;offset&gt; bytes from the current position.</td>
 </tr>
 <tr>
  <th>&lt;origin&gt;</th>
  <td>2</td>
  <td>&lt;offset&gt; bytes from the end of the file.</td>
 </tr>
</table>

## Example

```ttl
; Move to the beginning of file.
fileseek fhandle 0 0

; Move 10 bytes from the current position.
fileseek fhandle 10 1

; Move to the end of file.
fileseek fhandle 0 2

; Move to the position 10 bytes backward from the end of file.
fileseek fhandle 0-10 2
```
